### Observed differences

- Participation did not change: each of A15, A16, A17, A19, A20, A21, A22, A23, A24 and A25 occurs in all 200 traces in both windows, and every qualified activity pair co-occurs in 100% of traces in both windows. The differences below are therefore about ordering, not about activities appearing or disappearing. [POS001–POS010, REL001–REL022]

- In the earlier window, the relative order of the two activity groups varied from case to case: for example, A15 preceded A21 in only about 23 in 100 traces, A20 preceded A21 in about 3 in 100, while A15 preceded A23 in about 58 in 100 — every cross-group pair took both orders. In the later window, all 22 qualified cross-group pairs run in a single direction in 100% of traces: the A15/A16/A17/A19/A20-side activity comes before the A21–A25-side activity in every trace. [REL001–REL022]

- Outgoing transitions were re-focused within groups. Earlier, A15 sent about 49 in 100 of its outgoing transitions to A21–A25 and the rest to A15/A16/A17/A20; in the later window its transitions go only to A16 (about 36 in 100), A20 (about 32) and A17 (about 32). Three fixed bridges emerged: A20 now leads only to A21 (100% of its transitions, versus about 3 in 100 earlier), A22 only to A31 (100% versus about 50), and A30 only to A19 (100% versus about 54). [DIR001, DIR002, DIR004, DIR006, DIR010]

- Distances collapsed. Within-group neighbours became adjacent: A15→A16 is now always 1–2 steps apart (about 69 in 100 at distance 1) against a spread over 1–5 earlier. Cross-group gaps became fixed: A19→A21 and A20→A22 are now always exactly 5 steps (earlier spread over 1–5), and A22→A31 and A30→A19 are always 1 step. Pairs that were rarely close earlier now always are: A20→A24 within five steps in about 28 of 200 traces earlier, in all 200 later. [LAG001, LAG026, LAG027, LAG029, LAG035, LAG051]

- Event positions shifted consistently: A15, A16 and A17 moved earlier (mean position from about 0.61 to about 0.55), A20 from about 0.71 to about 0.61, while A21 moved later (about 0.53 to about 0.63), A23/A24/A25 from about 0.61 to about 0.68, and A22 to about 0.74; the case-to-case spread narrowed for all of them. [POS001–POS010]

- In the later window the behaviour is consistent with one fixed chain — A30, A19, then A15/A16/A17 in varying order, then A20, A21, then A23/A24/A25 in varying order, then A22, A31 — while order inside each block still varies (e.g., A23→A24 and A24→A23 both occur at 1–2 steps). [LAG037, LAG041, LAG045, DIR004, DIR006, DIR010]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports one main hypothesis: a reordering of the process — in the earlier window the group A15, A16, A17, A20 and the group A21, A22, A23, A24, A25 (with A30/A19 upstream and A31 downstream) were executed in case-specific, partly interleaved orders, whereas in the later window they follow one fixed block sequence (A30 → A19 → A15/A16/A17 in varying order → A20 → A21 → A23/A24/A25 in varying order → A22 → A31). This is a change in ordering constraints — from a mixed order to a fixed order — not an exchange of positions and not a change in participation, since every involved activity appears in all traces of both windows. [REL001–REL022, DIR001–DIR010, POS001–POS010]

The support is direct and consistent: the relational items show the change outright (mixed orders earlier, a single order in 100% of later traces for all 22 pairs), the successor profiles and inter-event distances change exactly as this reordering implies, and the screening flagged 93 control-flow items where fewer than one (about 0.72) would be expected without a change; each item's difference is also larger than in about 995 of 1000 random re-splits of the pooled data. [REL001–REL022, DIR001–DIR010, LAG001–LAG051]

Limitations: the qualified items describe largely the same traces, so they represent one coherent difference rather than many independent confirmations; and the evidence cannot fully rule out that the earlier window mixed several coexisting ordering variants that later collapsed into one dominant sequence, although the pair-specific, broadly spread order shares (about 3 to about 80 in 100) fit flexible interleaving better than a small set of fixed variants. Positions and distances are event-position based, so no claim about clock-time timing is made. [REL001–REL022, POS001–POS010]

Other differences: none outside this reordering — participation stayed at 100% for every tracked activity in both windows, and the position shifts and distance changes are facets of the same reordering. [POS001–POS010, LAG001–LAG051]
